title: Faizul Kabir
text:
I am a PhD candidate in the Department of Agricultural Economics at the University of Nebraska–Lincoln. My work broadly lies in environmental and resource economics and behavioral economics, with a focus on how producers and consumers make adoption decisions.
I am currently studying ranchers’ preferences for the Grassland Conservation Reserve Program (CRP) and the role of social networks in conservation program participation and practice adoption in the Northern U.S. Great Plains. Going forward, I want to extend this work to settings where policy design shapes the adoption of agricultural, food, and conservation programs and practices.
I am currently on the job market and open to opportunities in research, policy, and academia.

title: Research
text: My research examines producer decision-making in grassland conservation: preferences for the Grassland CRP (discrete choice experiments), the role of ego-networks in program participation, and the determinants of practices such as rotational grazing.
